name: Learn: Helm & Kustomize
objective: CKAD › Application Deployment. Drill EVERY Helm and Kustomize corner harder than the exam: scaffold+install a release, override values with --set and a values file, inspect release state and revisions, render without installing, apply a Kustomize base, layer transforms (namePrefix + commonLabels + replicas), generate a ConfigMap, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.
description: Nine strict practicals across the whole Helm + Kustomize surface. Each Check shows which requirements you met and the exact reason for any you missed.

questions.title: Helm: scaffold a chart and install a release
questions.teach:
**Helm** packages manifests as a **chart** and each deployment as a **release**. `helm create <name>` scaffolds a chart; `helm install <release> <chart> -n <ns>` renders and applies it. The default chart names its Deployment `<release>-<chart>`, so here it is `demo-webapp`.

**Gotcha:** plain `helm install` fails if the release name already exists — `helm upgrade --install` is the idempotent form.
questions.prompt:
Namespace `helm-learn` already exists. Scaffold a chart named `webapp` on the host (e.g. `cd /tmp && helm create webapp`), then install a release named `demo` of it into `helm-learn`.

Target: a release Secret of type `helm.sh/release.v1` for release `demo` exists in `helm-learn`, AND the chart's Deployment `demo-webapp` is present there.
questions.hint: `cd /tmp && helm create webapp`, then `helm install demo /tmp/webapp -n helm-learn`. Check with `helm list -n helm-learn` and `kubectl get deploy demo-webapp -n helm-learn`.
questions.solution:
cd /tmp
helm create webapp
helm install demo /tmp/webapp -n helm-learn
helm list -n helm-learn
kubectl get deploy demo-webapp -n helm-learn

verification.description: helm release 'demo' Secret (helm.sh/release.v1) and Deployment demo-webapp exist in helm-learn

questions.title: Helm: override a value on upgrade (--set)
questions.teach:
Charts expose knobs through **values**. Override one without editing chart files via `helm upgrade <release> <chart> --set <key>=<value>` — Helm re-renders and patches the live objects. The default chart's `replicaCount` flows into the Deployment's `spec.replicas`.

**Gotcha:** `helm upgrade` still needs the chart reference (`helm upgrade demo /tmp/webapp ...`), not just the release name.
questions.prompt:
Upgrade the `demo` release so its Deployment runs **4** replicas, by overriding `replicaCount` with `--set` (do not edit the chart files).

Target: Deployment `demo-webapp` in `helm-learn` has `spec.replicas: 4`.
questions.hint: `helm upgrade demo /tmp/webapp -n helm-learn --set replicaCount=4`, then `kubectl get deploy demo-webapp -n helm-learn -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}'`.
questions.solution:
helm upgrade demo /tmp/webapp -n helm-learn --set replicaCount=4
kubectl get deploy demo-webapp -n helm-learn -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}'   # 4

verification.description: demo-webapp Deployment scaled to 4 replicas via helm --set

questions.title: Helm: override the image tag with a values file
questions.teach:
For many or persistent overrides, write a YAML **values file** and pass it with `-f`: `helm upgrade <release> <chart> -f values.override.yaml`. Keys mirror the chart's `values.yaml` structure. The default chart maps `image.tag` into the container image as `<repository>:<tag>`.

**Gotcha:** `-f` and `--set` can combine, and `--set` wins — on a tie the command-line value overrides the file.
questions.prompt:
Still overriding (not editing the chart): set the `demo` release's container image **tag** to `1.25` using a **values file** (`-f`). The default chart's image repository is `nginx`, so the container image becomes `nginx:1.25`.

Target: the first container of Deployment `demo-webapp` in `helm-learn` has image ending in `:1.25` (i.e. `nginx:1.25`). Keep replicas at 4.
questions.hint: Write `/tmp/override.yaml` with `image:\n  tag: "1.25"`, then `helm upgrade demo /tmp/webapp -n helm-learn -f /tmp/override.yaml --set replicaCount=4`. Verify the container image: `kubectl get deploy demo-webapp -n helm-learn -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'`.
questions.solution:
cat > /tmp/override.yaml <<'YAML'
image:
  tag: "1.25"
YAML
helm upgrade demo /tmp/webapp -n helm-learn -f /tmp/override.yaml --set replicaCount=4
kubectl get deploy demo-webapp -n helm-learn -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'   # nginx:1.25

verification.description: demo-webapp container image tag is 1.25 (via -f values file), replicas still 4

questions.title: Helm: inspect release state and revision
questions.teach:
`helm list -n <ns>` shows each release with its status and **revision** number; every `install`/`upgrade` bumps the revision. A status of `deployed` (not `failed`/`superseded`) confirms the last operation succeeded. The current revision's state lives in a Secret labelled `status=deployed`.

**Gotcha:** `helm list`/`status` are namespace-scoped — omit `-n <ns>` and a release looks "missing"; use `-A` when unsure.
questions.prompt:
After two upgrades, confirm the `demo` release is **deployed** and now on **revision 3** in `helm-learn`.

Target: the deployed-state release Secret for `demo` carries labels `status=deployed` and `version=3` (`helm list -n helm-learn` shows REVISION 3, STATUS deployed).
questions.hint: `helm list -n helm-learn` → REVISION 3, STATUS deployed. The deployed state Secret is labelled `owner=helm,status=deployed,name=demo,version=3`: `kubectl get secret -n helm-learn -l owner=helm,status=deployed,name=demo --show-labels`.
questions.solution:
helm list -n helm-learn
helm status demo -n helm-learn
kubectl get secret -n helm-learn -l owner=helm,status=deployed,name=demo -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.labels.version}'   # 3

verification.description: release 'demo' is deployed and on revision 3 in helm-learn

questions.title: Helm: render a chart without installing (template)
questions.teach:
`helm template <name> <chart>` renders a chart's manifests to stdout **without touching the cluster** — the way to preview or pipe YAML into `kubectl`. `--set`/`-f` apply during render just like on install, so you can verify an override before shipping it.

**Gotcha:** `helm template` does NOT create a release or run server-side — nothing appears in `helm list`; it is purely local rendering.
questions.prompt:
Without creating a release, render your `webapp` chart with `replicaCount=7` and write the output to `/tmp/rendered.yaml` on the host.

Target: file `/tmp/rendered.yaml` exists and contains a Deployment manifest whose rendered `replicas: 7` (and no new release appears in `helm-learn`).

verification.description: /tmp/rendered.yaml contains a rendered Deployment with replicas: 7 (no install performed)

questions.title: Kustomize: apply a base
questions.teach:
**Kustomize** customizes plain manifests with **no templating**: a `kustomization.yaml` lists `resources` and transforms. `kubectl apply -k <dir>` builds that kustomization and applies it. The base at `/tmp/kustomize-ckad` has Deployment `hello` and pins `namespace: kustomize-learn`.

**Gotcha:** `-k` takes a **directory** (or git URL), not a file — `kubectl apply -k ./dir`, never `-k file.yaml`.
questions.prompt:
Apply the Kustomize base at `/tmp/kustomize-ckad` to the cluster.

Target: Deployment `hello` exists in namespace `kustomize-learn`.
questions.solution:
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad
kubectl get deploy hello -n kustomize-learn

verification.description: Deployment 'hello' created in kustomize-learn from the base

questions.title: Kustomize: namePrefix + commonLabels + replicas
questions.teach:
Kustomize transforms rewrite the built output without copying YAML. `namePrefix:` prepends to every resource name, `commonLabels:` stamps a label onto every resource (and selectors), and a `replicas:` entry patches a named workload's replica count.

**Gotcha:** `commonLabels` also rewrites the Deployment's **selector** — immutable once created, so a label added later to a live Deployment can force a recreate.
questions.prompt:
Edit `/tmp/kustomize-ckad/kustomization.yaml` to add three transforms, then re-apply with `kubectl apply -k`:
- `namePrefix: prod-` (Deployment becomes `prod-hello`)
- `commonLabels: {tier: frontend}`
- `replicas:` set workload `hello` to **5**

Target: Deployment `prod-hello` exists in `kustomize-learn` with label `tier=frontend` and `spec.replicas: 5`.
questions.hint:
Add `namePrefix: prod-`, `commonLabels:
  tier: frontend`, and `replicas:
- name: hello
  count: 5` to the kustomization, then `kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad`. Verify: `kubectl get deploy prod-hello -n kustomize-learn -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.tier} {.spec.replicas}'`.
questions.solution:
cat >> /tmp/kustomize-ckad/kustomization.yaml <<'YAML'
namePrefix: prod-
commonLabels:
  tier: frontend
replicas:
- name: hello
  count: 5
YAML
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad
kubectl get deploy prod-hello -n kustomize-learn -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.tier} {.spec.replicas}'   # frontend 5

verification.description: prod-hello in kustomize-learn has label tier=frontend and replicas 5

questions.title: Kustomize: generate a ConfigMap
questions.teach:
`configMapGenerator` builds a ConfigMap from literals or files, appending a content **hash** suffix to its name so a data change forces a rollout. `generatorOptions: {disableNameSuffixHash: true}` keeps a stable name when you need to reference it by a fixed value.

**Gotcha:** the generated name also picks up `namePrefix`, so with `namePrefix: prod-` the ConfigMap `app-cfg` becomes `prod-app-cfg` (plus the hash unless disabled).
questions.prompt:
Add a `configMapGenerator` to `/tmp/kustomize-ckad/kustomization.yaml` that creates ConfigMap `app-cfg` with literal `GREETING=hello`, and disable the name-hash suffix (`generatorOptions`). Re-apply with `kubectl apply -k`.

Target: a ConfigMap named `prod-app-cfg` (namePrefix applied, hash disabled) exists in `kustomize-learn` with `data.GREETING=hello`.
questions.hint:
Append `configMapGenerator:
- name: app-cfg
  literals:
  - GREETING=hello` and `generatorOptions:
  disableNameSuffixHash: true`. With the existing `namePrefix: prod-` the result is `prod-app-cfg`. Verify: `kubectl get cm prod-app-cfg -n kustomize-learn -o jsonpath='{.data.GREETING}'`.
questions.solution:
cat >> /tmp/kustomize-ckad/kustomization.yaml <<'YAML'
configMapGenerator:
- name: app-cfg
  literals:
  - GREETING=hello
generatorOptions:
  disableNameSuffixHash: true
YAML
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad
kubectl get cm prod-app-cfg -n kustomize-learn -o jsonpath='{.data.GREETING}'   # hello

verification.description: ConfigMap prod-app-cfg (hash disabled) in kustomize-learn has GREETING=hello

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a broken kustomization
questions.teach:
`kubectl apply -k <dir>` first **builds** the kustomization; if the build fails, nothing is applied and you get an error instead of resources. The usual causes: a `resources:` entry naming a file that doesn't exist, or a bad transform value.

**Gotcha:** read the build error first (`kubectl kustomize <dir>`) — it names the exact missing file or field before anything reaches the cluster.
questions.prompt:
The kustomization at `/tmp/kustomize-broken` **won't build** — `kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-broken` errors and applies nothing. Diagnose the fault and fix the kustomization so the build succeeds and its Deployment is applied. Don't rewrite it from scratch — find and fix what's wrong.

Target: Deployment `api` exists in namespace `kustomize-learn` (built from the fixed `/tmp/kustomize-broken`).
questions.hint: `kubectl kustomize /tmp/kustomize-broken` shows the build error — `resources:` lists `deploy.yaml` but the file on disk is `deployment.yaml` (or vice versa). Make the `resources:` entry match the real filename, then `kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-broken`.
questions.solution:
# Build error: resources points at a file that doesn't exist.
ls /tmp/kustomize-broken
kubectl kustomize /tmp/kustomize-broken   # shows the offending filename
# Fix the resources entry to the real file name, then:
sed -i 's/deploy.yaml/deployment.yaml/' /tmp/kustomize-broken/kustomization.yaml
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-broken
kubectl get deploy api -n kustomize-learn

verification.description: Deployment 'api' applied in kustomize-learn (broken kustomization fixed)
